author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Micron Technology said its direct labor employees in Taiwan will receive fiscal-year rewards worth between 35 and 68 months of pay, an unusually large compensation package for workers in the island’s semiconductor sector.

Each eligible employee is guaranteed at least T$1.7 million, about $53,800, in cash compensation, Reuters reported. Workers who joined Micron before August 29, 2025, are also set to receive an additional T$1 million cash bonus. The exact award varies by employee and eligibility.

The announcement follows strong support among union members for possible strike action. Unions represent roughly two-thirds of Micron’s Taiwan workforce, making labor relations a significant operational issue for a company that depends on the island for memory-chip production.

Micron did not characterize the rewards as a settlement of the labor dispute in the Reuters report. The package nevertheless increases the financial incentive for skilled employees to remain with the company at a time when demand for advanced memory used in AI systems has tightened supply chains. Any effect on negotiations, staffing or production will depend on the unions’ next steps.
dek: The chipmaker announced large fiscal-year compensation packages for direct labor employees after unions showed strong support for possible strike action.
headline: Micron’s Taiwan workers receive rewards worth up to 68 months of pay
